exposure: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA)
outcome: Maternal cardiovascular complications during pregnancy and childbirth
cohort: Women with ccTGA followed at a tertiary care center in Poland between April 1991 and April 2012
finding: Most women with ccTGA can achieve successful pregnancy, and while supraventricular arrhythmias are the most common cardiovascular complication, pregnancy does not appear to worsen right ventricular function in the long term.
mod_finding: Of the 19 successful deliveries, 14 (74%) were vaginal and 5 (26%) were cesarean.
